Summarise an sdmTMB cross-validation on a per-observation scale

Source: R/model-selection.R
sdmTMB_cv_summary.Rd

Turns an sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv() object into a one-row summary whose log-likelihood is expressed per held-out observation, together with the fold-level diagnostics needed to tell a clean comparison from a fragile one.

Usage

sdmTMB_cv_summary(x, label = NA_character_, response = NULL)

Arguments

x

An object of class sdmTMB_cv from sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(), or a try-error/NULL from a crashed run.

label

Optional character label carried into the model column.

response

Name of the response column, used for cv_RMSE/cv_MAE. If NULL (default), taken from the left-hand side of the fitted formula.

Value

A one-row tibble with model, folds, folds_pdhess, n_heldout, cv_loglik (per held-out observation; higher is better), cv_RMSE, cv_MAE and cv_crashed.

Details

A summed hold-out log-likelihood is not comparable between candidates that held out different numbers of observations. That happens more easily than it looks: candidates fitted to different complete-case subsets (see selection_frame()) hold out different numbers of rows, and a candidate that sums fewer terms scores higher, which inverts the ranking exactly where the comparison is least reliable. Dividing by the number of contributing observations removes the artefact; n_heldout is reported alongside so a row assembled from a different number of points is visible as such.

folds_pdhess counts the folds whose Hessian was positive definite. A fold with a non-positive-definite Hessian still yields point predictions, so it contributes to all three criteria while signalling that its optimum is not trustworthy — the count has to be shown or the reader cannot see it.

See also

sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(), sdmTMB_selection()

Author

Mikko Vihtakari

Examples

# \donttest{
mesh <- sdmTMB::make_mesh(sdmTMB::pcod, c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 25)
cv <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(
  density ~ 0 + as.factor(year), data = sdmTMB::pcod, mesh = mesh,
  family = sdmTMB::tweedie(), k_folds = 2
)
#> Running fits with `future.apply()`.
#> Set a parallel `future::plan()` to use parallel processing.
sdmTMB_cv_summary(cv, label = "Year only")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   model     folds folds_pdhess n_heldout cv_loglik cv_RMSE cv_MAE cv_crashed
#>   <chr>     <int>        <int>     <int>     <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> <lgl>     
#> 1 Year only     2            2      2143     -3.20    198.   52.6 FALSE     
# }
